memory_candidates.content: A lint's own bracket-depth matcher can treat a call's title-parens argument as bracket-neutral by construction, avoiding a separate body-open-bracket locator: if quoted-string contents are stripped from each line before counting brackets, a title argument like #remark("Title")[ contributes no stray '[' or ']' (since the only bracket left after quote-stripping is the body's own opening '['), so the whole line's net bracket delta from the point the call is first detected already equals the correct starting depth. This removes an entire class of parsing complexity (locating exactly where a body opens after an arbitrary title-argument list) for any 'find where a Typst/Lua/similar call's bracket body starts and ends' problem where title/keyword arguments are string-only.

When a new mechanical lint is validated against a corpus larger than its single motivating fixture, expect it to surface additional pre-existing instances of the same defect pattern across other files in the corpus -- this is a sign the lint generalizes correctly, not evidence of a false-positive bug. Before concluding a corpus-wide finding is a lint defect, manually inspect a representative sample of the newly-flagged instances against the source; only a finding that does NOT match the documented defect pattern (i.e., the rule's own literal wording) is a true false positive requiring a fix. Distinguishing 'the lint found more real violations than expected' from 'the lint has a bug' is the actual acceptance-validation question, and conflating the two risks either shipping a broken check or wrongly weakening a correct one.
